paper_context.label: first-divergence states (dev forks, 20 blocks), NOT the U2B panel: context only

reading: Not yet answerable: the strict primary admits one RTN block and two GPTQ blocks, so m24 within-divergent G−H (RTN +4.1 pp at k = 1, GPTQ +0.0 [−30.3, +30.3] at k = 2) and M1 carry no inferential weight, and every labelled k = 3 sensitivity (RTN −0.6 [−10.6, +9.6], GPTQ −4.5 [−17.8, +9.3] on available rows) and the complete BFCL panel (RTN −0.6 [−7.3, +5.9], GPTQ +0.0 [−6.2, +6.4]) contains both zero and the q8 point estimates. What does carry over descriptively is the shape around G−H: in Mistral as in Qwen3-8B, a quantized action changes the outcome at many divergent states (τ² within-divergent M 15 to 25 pp in m24 vs 16 to 17 pp in q8), net action value is small against that turnover (G_all +0.6 and +3.6 pp vs M 12.7 and 10.8 in m24; +0.4 and +2.7 vs 6.7 and 9.0 in q8), and roughly one divergent state in five has a controller-dependent action effect (off-diagonal 18 to 24 % vs 16.5 to 18.5 %). The q8 action-over-continuation advantage is resolved only on first-divergence states with 20 blocks; on this U2B panel q8 W4 also spans zero (+2.8 [−10.3, +14.7], +1.5 [−7.3, +10.1]) and the m24 GPTQ sensitivities lean negative, so the paper can report the replicated turnover structure but cannot yet say whether the G−H sign replicates in a second family.
